headline: FOMC MINUTES CONFIRM THREE DISSENTERS WANTED JULY HIKE — GOLD HOLDS $4,400 AS SEPTEMBER ODDS FALL TO 30%
snippet: The Federal Reserve's July 28–29 meeting minutes, released Wednesday August 19 at 2pm ET, confirmed that three FOMC members dissented in favor of an immediate rate hike — more hawkish than markets expected. Despite the tone, gold held above $4,400, with September hike probability collapsing from 57% at the time of the meeting to roughly 30% following three weeks of weak U.S. labor, inflation, and retail sales data. The minutes also revealed an active internal debate about whether AI-driven investment and supply shocks could entrench inflation pressures through 2027 — a structural argument that could matter for gold well beyond the September decision.

headline: ANTIMONY SUPPLY WALL: WEST MEETS ONLY 73% OF NON-CHINA DEMAND BY 2030 — EVEN IF EVERY PROJECT GETS BUILT
snippet: A new GlobeNewswire research report published August 19 finds that Western antimony smelters — assuming every announced project is built and permitted on schedule — can only meet roughly 73% of non-China demand by 2030, leaving a structural shortfall of more than a quarter of the market. The U.S. has had zero domestic antimony production since 1942 and imported 91% of its supply in 2025. Despite nearly $400 million in committed federal investment, no domestic mine will produce antimony before late 2028. China imposed export licensing requirements in August 2024 and an outright ban on U.S. shipments in December 2024, driving prices to an all-time record of $59,750/tonne by mid-2025. For junior mining investors, this is the clearest example of a structural supply deficit that governments have explicitly committed to funding their way out of.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,400 FLOOR AFTER HAWKISH MINUTES — STRUCTURAL BULL TREND INTACT ABOVE KEY SUPPORT
snippet: Despite the July FOMC minutes confirming a hawkish minority of three dissenters, gold maintained support above the $4,400 level in Wednesday's session — a technically significant hold that analysts argue validates the medium-term bull structure. Gold climbed more than $320 from its post-FOMC low of $4,072 to $4,392 in three weeks on weakening U.S. economic data; the minutes, rather than resetting that recovery, appear to have confirmed that the Fed majority remains cautious about hiking into a softening labor market. The analysis argues that $4,400 on a weekly close is the line in the sand — and gold held it.

headline: AMERICAN EAGLE GOLD NAK: 1,001 METRES OF 0.46% CuEq FROM SURFACE — LONGEST INTERCEPT EVER DRILLED AT B.C. COPPER PROJECT
snippet: American Eagle Gold Corp. (TSXV: AE, OTCQB: AMEGF) announced August 18 that step-out hole NAK26-87 at its NAK copper-gold project in British Columbia intersected 1,001 metres of 0.46% CuEq starting at surface — the longest mineralized intercept ever drilled at NAK — including a high-grade core of 218 metres at 1.01% CuEq. The kilometre-long intercept starting from surface significantly lowers the strip ratio assumption for future pit designs, a critical variable for capital intensity in large-tonnage open-pit porphyry deposits. At $6.60 copper and $4,400 gold, a system that delivers 1% CuEq over 218 metres from surface in British Columbia is exactly the kind of discovery that attracts strategic investment from major copper producers actively replacing depleting reserves.

headline: SILVER JUMPS 2% ABOVE $66 — THREE STRAIGHT GAINS AS FED RATE-HIKE BETS EVAPORATE ON WEAK U.S. DATA
snippet: Silver accelerated above $66/oz on Monday August 17, jumping over 2% as the U.S. dollar weakened sharply following soft retail sales and labor market data that pushed the probability of a September Federal Reserve rate hike to roughly 30% — down from 57% on the day of the July FOMC decision. Silver has now gained approximately 14% in August versus gold's 9%, compressing the gold-silver ratio to 67 from above 72 in late July, as industrial demand from solar panel manufacturing, EV components, and AI data center infrastructure adds a physical bid beneath the monetary-metals rally. Markets are no longer fully pricing a rate increase by year-end, unlike just a week ago.

headline: THIS WEEK IN GOLD: FOMC MINUTES, AUGUST PMI FLASH, PHILLY FED — THREE DATA POINTS THAT DECIDE THE NEXT MOVE
snippet: This week's macro calendar is unusually dense for gold investors: FOMC minutes from the hawkish July 28–29 meeting arrive Wednesday (August 19), followed by the Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index and July industrial production on Thursday, and the August preliminary PMI flash for both manufacturing and services on Friday. Each data point feeds the September rate-hike debate that is currently the primary driver of gold's short-term direction. A dovish or neutral read from the minutes combined with soft PMI data would reinforce gold's $4,400 support hold; a hawkish surprise in either direction could test the level before the metal regains footing on the medium-term bull thesis.

headline: J.P. MORGAN: GOLD AVERAGES $5,055 IN Q4 2026 — BULL CASE STRETCHES TO $6,000, MINERS TO OUTPERFORM BULLION
snippet: J.P. Morgan's latest commodity team forecast — one of the most-cited on the street — projects gold averaging $5,055 per ounce in Q4 2026, with a bull case that stretches to $6,000 under sustained safe-haven demand and continued Fed caution. The Canadian Mining Report notes that junior and mid-tier gold mining stocks are still trading at historically cheap valuations despite delivering record operating margins at $4,300–$4,400 gold, creating conditions where earnings leverage to sustained high prices has yet to fully flow through to share prices — the same dynamic driving the GDX's August outperformance. If gold prices remain at current levels or rise toward J.P. Morgan's target, today's share prices still do not reflect those higher price assumptions.

headline: KORYX COPPER HAIB: HIGHEST GRADES EVER RECORDED — 8.01% Cu AND 60.5 g/t Ag IN 17-HOLE NAMIBIA DRILL BATCH
snippet: Koryx Copper (TSXV: KRY) reported August 14 results from 17 drill holes (6,430 metres) at its wholly-owned Haib copper-molybdenum-gold porphyry project in southern Namibia, with the batch including the highest copper (8.01% Cu) and silver (60.5 g/t Ag) grades ever recorded at Haib from surface intercept HMRC008. The results demonstrate the highly consistent nature of copper mineralization across Haib's large-scale disseminated system, with significant molybdenum and gold byproduct credits, while 14 drill rigs remain active on site. Haib is envisaged as a large-scale open-pit mine producing a Cu-Mo concentrate with potential additional copper cathode production via oxide heap leaching — exactly the kind of development-stage copper asset that base-metals majors need to replace reserves at $6.60 copper.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION GOODWIN: MASSIVE SULPHIDE FOUND 2,000 METRES NORTHWEST OF KNOWN ZONES — 24.6 METRES AT 1.19% CuEq
snippet: SLAM Exploration Ltd. (TSXV: SXL) announced August 14 that hole GW26-29 at the Goodwin copper-nickel-cobalt project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp returned 24.60 metres grading 1.19% CuEq from a massive sulphide zone, while a separate hole 2,000 metres northwest of the known Logan zone discovered new massive sulphide intervals hosted in coarse-grained gabbro — significantly expanding the project's footprint. The Bathurst Mining Camp is one of Canada's most prolific historical base-metals districts, home to legacy Noranda and Falconbridge operations, and SLAM's 2026 campaign — funded in part by a $60,000 Province of New Brunswick grant — is testing multiple VTEM geophysical targets along a 2,000-metre strike corridor adjacent to known high-grade zones. A discovery step-out that opens a new 2,000-metre corridor in a proven camp is among the highest-optionality events in junior exploration.

headline: AuAg FUNDS: 'RIDING A BULL ISN'T FOR THE FAINT OF HEART' — WHAT COMES NEXT FOR GOLD PRODUCERS ABOVE $4,400
snippet: European precious metals fund manager AuAg Funds publishes its 2026 gold and gold miners outlook, arguing that the macro tailwind for gold has rarely been stronger while the operational and geopolitical ground beneath producers has never felt less predictable — a combination that rewards careful stock selection over passive ETF exposure. The analysis notes that gold miners are caught between surging long-term yields, shifting monetary policy regimes, and a fragile geopolitical landscape, yet are delivering record cash flows and beginning to return capital to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. The core argument: today's re-rating is just beginning, but volatile price action is the cost of entry into the trade that took precious metals from $2,000 to $4,400.
